children: U.S. infrastructure services firm's Q3 revenue declined 10.4% yr/yr but met analyst expectations
Adjusted EPS for Q3 beat analyst expectations
Company's board authorized new $250 mln share repurchase program on October 30
Primoris sees 2026 net income between $65.2 mln and $73.2 mln
Company expects 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.10 to $2.25
Primoris forecasts 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $290 mln to $310 mln
RENEWABLES SLOWDOWN - Lower renewables revenue in the Energy segment was the main reason for the revenue decline, partially offset by growth in Utilities segment
PROJECT DELAYS - Co cited slower than anticipated start of new renewables projects and release of new work in the Energy segment
OPERATIONAL CHALLENGES - Lagging effects from renewables projects with operational challenges and lower volumes increased costs in the Energy segment
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 12 "strong buy" or "buy", 6 "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the construction & engineering peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Primoris Services Corporation is $106.66, about 44.5% above its November 2 closing price of $73.79
The stock recently traded at 16 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 20 three months ago
